buyBody: Heavy, honest, and milled from 431 stainless. A blade for the golfer who wants to know exactly where the putt came off the face. Right hand, and sold out at the moment.

whatYouGet: One Tracer LGP01 Blade putter, right hand
No headcover (none of our clubs ship with one)
clubHeadline: A smaller head tells you more. Roll it pure.
clubParas: A blade is a choice. Less help on the miss, and in return it tells you exactly where on the face you hit it, every single time. The Tracer Blade is CNC-milled 431 stainless, muted and solid off the face with no ping, and heavy for a blade at 385 grams so it stays planted through a four-footer when your hands want to get involved. If you'd rather know than be forgiven, this is your putter.

clubSpecs.v: Muted and solid at impact. No ring, no ping, no buzz through the hands, and honest feedback on the ones you miss.
One-piece 431 stainless head, milled face, 3.5° of loft and 385 g at 35 inches. Gold finish, Lucky rubber grip.
Players who release the head through the stroke and want to know about a miss, not have it covered up.

videoBrief: 16:9 product film, 40–60s. Down-the-line showing the arc the head wants to travel on, then the face at impact in slow motion. A blade's argument is feel, which is the hardest thing to film. Lean on sound.
specSub: 385 grams, 3.5 degrees of loft, 35 inches, right hand. The whole sheet.

look.headline: Less club, more information
paras: Most blades are chrome and try to disappear. This one is gold, 385 grams, and has no interest in disappearing.
A small head that doesn't go unnoticed. Your playing partners will see it before they see the stroke.
If you would rather the head covered the miss, the Tracer Mallet is the other one.

helpPick.headline: Both suit an arc. The question is feel or forgiveness.
helpPick.sub: Normally it's mallets for straight strokes and blades for arcs. Not here: both Tracers are built for a stroke with some arc in it. The real question is how much you want the head to help on the ones you miss, and how much you want it to tell you.

options.name: Tracer Blade
options.body: For players who release the head through the stroke. Twenty grams heavier and far less forgiving. The trade is that a blade tells you exactly where on the face you hit it.

options.name: Tracer Mallet
options.body: Slight toe hang from a plumber neck, so it works with the arc you already have. Perimeter weighting keeps an off-center strike on line. You give up some feedback to get that.

helpPick.note: The blade is out of stock and right hand only when it returns. If you want the feedback rather than the forgiveness, that is worth waiting for.

_club: Fourth pass, 2026-08-19. Cole: 'I feel like you're using the same structure over and over again.' He was right: every intro opened material -> 'so it feels' -> feature -> 'so it' -> spec line. Takomo's intros each open through a different door (a situation, a joke, a problem, a brag, a sibling). THIS ONE OPENS WITH: the choice a blade is.

clubGrinds.v: Twenty grams more than the mallet. That extra weight is what stops the face twisting on a short one and keeps your hands out of the stroke.
The stock Lucky rubber grip, not the oversized 3.0 on the mallet. An arcing stroke wants to feel the club, and a fat grip takes that away.

_specTabs: Takomo-shaped 2026-08-19 to match the Gold: three cards (Clubs / Shafts / Grips), each a caption, a stacked key/value head and a black-header matrix. A putter has one loft and one length, so the Clubs matrix runs the four figures as COLUMNS against one head-shape row rather than lofts as columns. The old shape was Club / Shaft & grip. specSub used to name "the Product Reference Guide v1.8" in customer-facing text: an internal document and its version number, on the page.
